topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames complement as an important but nomenclaturally complicated subject and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic molecular framework for understanding how inactive complement proteins become active immune effectors.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition produces concentrated surface-bound C3b sufficient to trigger complement activity.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement promotes the elimination of pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activity to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects the functions of particular complement components to the distinct clinical consequences of their deficiency.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how pathogens evade complement, including how the antibody-binding activity of staphylococcal protein A can be repurposed clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and announces adaptive immunity as the next subject.
